finding.claim: A malicious or compromised MCP server can make the client send unauthenticated GET requests to attacker-chosen loopback http and arbitrary https hosts via the resource_metadata URL in WWW-Authenticate. The response is not returned to the attacker, so the impact is blind SSRF: reachability oracle and GET side effects on internal services.
finding.source: WWW-Authenticate resource_metadata parameter in a 401/403 response from the MCP server (lib/mcp/client/http.rb:465-469 parse_www_authenticate_from_error)
finding.sink: http_get(url) in lib/mcp/client/oauth/flow.rb:764-766, a Faraday GET to the attacker-supplied URL

trace.note: run_oauth_flow! takes params from the 401 WWW-Authenticate header
attempt_refresh also forwards resource_metadata_url to flow.refresh!
secure_url? allows any https host and http loopback hosts (127.0.0.0/8, ::1, localhost)
fetch_protected_resource_metadata builds candidates with the attacker URL first
protected_resource_metadata_urls puts resource_metadata_url at the front of the list
locate_authorization_server rescues AuthorizationError and discards the PRM error, so no response content is surfaced
http_get issues the GET with no timeout and no IP or private-range filtering

finding.guards_checked: secure_url? requires https or loopback http only; no private, RFC1918, or link-local block; no resolved-IP pinning; no redirect control (Faraday does not follow redirects by default); no auth headers sent on the discovery GET; PRM errors swallowed at flow.rb:226-233, so no body read-back. Severity low to medium. Static reading only; not run.

finding.claim: The client_credentials client_secret is sent as HTTP Basic credentials to a token_endpoint chosen by the MCP server through PRM authorization_servers, with no binding between the configured credential and the authorization server it is sent to.
finding.source: PRM document (authorization_servers[0] and the AS metadata token_endpoint), reached via the attacker-controlled resource_metadata URL or by the malicious server itself
finding.sink: post_to_token_endpoint sends Authorization: Basic base64(client_id:client_secret) to token_endpoint (lib/mcp/client/oauth/flow.rb:696 and :707)

trace.note: locate_authorization_server takes the first authorization_servers entry from the PRM
issuer equals discovery URL, which an attacker AS trivially satisfies
post_to_token_endpoint loads client_id and client_secret from client_information
client_secret is base64-encoded into the Authorization header
http_post_form posts to the attacker-chosen token_endpoint
the client_secret was stored from developer config

finding.guards_checked: ensure_secure_endpoints! requires https on token_endpoint; resource_covers? (flow.rb:513-525) checks PRM resource only when PRM advertises it, so omitting it bypasses the check; issuer check passes for attacker AS; no pinning of AS to developer configuration. Precondition: malicious or compromised MCP server. Impact: disclosure of a long-lived client secret. Partly a design-trust question per MCP spec (PRM may name the AS); severity low to medium. Static reading only; not run.
